feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear positioning for senior digital communications/strategy roles and credible progression within one organization. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the header and experience consistently position you as a digital strategy, content, and platform modernization leader.  
- Credible career progression: multiple promotions at NACo show growth, trust, and increasing scope of responsibility.  
- Good specificity: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Clarity, Power BI, studio buildout, and website scale add credibility and technical depth.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; keep serial commas consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); standardize punctuation in bullets. No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and scope, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around leadership, modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector impact would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change to “12+ years of experience” and lead with your current level: “Digital communications and strategy leader…”
- Replace broad channel list with higher-value outcomes: enterprise web modernization, editorial systems, analytics, and cross-channel governance.
- Add sector relevance from the CV context, e.g., “mission-driven, membership, and public-sector organizations.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven and public-sector organizations. Brings deep expertise in enterprise web modernization, editorial operations, analytics, and platform governance across web, email, social, and multimedia. Known for translating complex policy and technical issues into clear content and building the systems, workflows, and stakeholder alignment needed to scale effective communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language duplicate Core Competencies; keep the intro more positioning-focused.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with Topline Skills; consider broadening to “policy and stakeholder communications.”
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, resume-style noun phrases and pluralize where appropriate: “Multi-channel communications,” not “communication.”
- Replace generic items with sharper, senior-level terms: “Web governance & CMS administration” and “Editorial systems & workflow design” are stronger than the current wording.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications • Web governance & CMS administration • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- If space allows, swap in one more differentiator from recent work, such as “AI-enabled search strategy” or “Platform modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with Topline Skills and Technical + IT; combining it with editorial/workflow language may reduce repetition.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace task-heavy bullets with 3–4 outcome-oriented bullets; e.g., “Redesigned Drupal campaign architecture with modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Combine overlapping execution points: merge CMS development, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting into one concise bullet focused on improving public-facing web performance/usability.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, teams/stakeholders served, workflow time reduced, search relevance gains, or engagement/conversion improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and organization-wide communications” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- AI search and microsite details also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level unless you add distinct outcomes.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine and tighten the website bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Reframe channel oversight around strategy/results, not routine management: “Oversaw enterprise email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, aligning channel strategy with advocacy and member communications goals.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting cadence, efficiency gains, engagement growth, or reduced reliance on vendors for the studio/analytics/governance bullets.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Current email/newsletter and video language overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on leadership, systems, and enterprise-scale transformation.
- “Governance/operations/workflows” also appears in the current consultant role; differentiate this entry with concrete transformation outcomes.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads a bit generic and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles before and after it. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what was established or scaled during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to show scope and contribution: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video accomplishment as a build/launch: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications channels” and “publishing workflows/governance” are already covered in the Director of Digital Media role; keep this entry focused on hands-on execution and channel-building.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the earlier 2015–2018 role; distinguish this one as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong theme alignment with the candidate’s recent leadership roles, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen executive-level strengths and use more distinctive phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive language:  
  **- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization**  
  **- Editorial governance and content operations**  
  **- Cross-channel communications leadership**  
  **- Public-sector and advocacy communications**  
  **- Audience strategy and content planning**
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “cross-channel communications leadership” to sound more current and concise.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker than the rest; “audience strategy and content planning” signals more senior ownership.
- If space allows, make one line more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat almost verbatim from the header/Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than listing every platform/language.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or older items unless they are job-target critical: consider removing jQuery first.
- Keep the most relevant recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If possible, align wording to proven outcomes elsewhere: “enterprise CMS modernization,” “large public-facing web properties,” or “structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; mention it once here only if it remains a target differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and business impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Leadership reporting • User behavior analysis • SEO and performance optimization”
- If you want to keep tools, limit to 2–3 most credible anchors: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio” rather than listing every platform.
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure • KPI design • Executive dashboards • GA4, BigQuery and BI reporting • User behavior insights • SEO/performance optimization”
- Use wording that matches recent experience: “reporting infrastructure” and “strategic decision-making” align well with the Director role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; vary the phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and use sharper phrasing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize current/relevant platforms or add light context on level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, proven platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, group by strength/relevance: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint/Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Remove weaker/older tools if they are not materially supported elsewhere; Drupal should clearly lead given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Keep formatting parallel with other technical lists; avoid adding too many niche qualifiers here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same CMS tools plus modernization context.
- Consider deleting this item entirely if the Topline Skills section remains, or use this section for tools not named elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools tied to recent work and grouping older/basic skills more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “JavaScript/jQuery • HTML/CSS • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Put the strongest, more distinctive tools first; HTML5/CSS3 can be simplified to “HTML/CSS” for concision.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere in recent roles rather than here, e.g., GTM for analytics deployment, Workers for edge logic, GitHub Actions for deployment automation.
- Consider renaming the category to “Front-End & Implementation Tools” to sound more senior and less like entry-level coding skills.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears in Topline Skills; keep it in one place or shorten one version.
- “API integrations” and automation themes also overlap with Core Competencies and “Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and signal level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant systems: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana**
- Move general collaboration apps to a separate lighter line only if space allows: **Slack • Teams**
- Drop older/lower-signal tools unless central to target roles: **Basecamp, Trello**; consider adding context only if true, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana (cross-team delivery)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools and may dilute the technical signal of this section.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and emphasize platform scope rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** only if these are true hands-on systems you configured or administered.
- If you want more signal, use: **Email marketing automation & member engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys, Higher Logic, Mailchimp**
- Keep naming consistent and current: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys” is strong; avoid mixing legacy product names elsewhere.
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency and depth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; don’t add “email campaigns/newsletters” wording here.
- “Engagement” may feel vague unless supported elsewhere; platform names alone may be cleaner.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, platform refresh, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles as part of NACo’s first in-house digital team, helping build day-to-day operations across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Replace “strengthening workflows” with clearer actions: “standardized publishing and production workflows” or “helped formalize cross-channel content processes.”
- Tighten the second sentence to concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, website size, or team size supervised.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this role as launching or piloting the format rather than expanding it.
- “providing day-to-day guidance” is weaker than later leadership bullets; keep it light to avoid overstating management at this stage.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital content roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast the anchor accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific support statement if true, e.g., “Produced digital and multimedia assets to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or programs/policy teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content/video work already covered in 2015–2024 roles.
- “First podcast” is distinctive; keep that, but don’t repeat later multimedia leadership language here.
